plain_summary: This page freezes what the project's records showed at 2026-11-25T23:59:59Z and explains what they mean. It looked at 152 groups of optimizer results (11 of them checked for use in training) and 25 carefully simulated horn designs.

Two nearly identical horn designs score almost the same, but only one meets the agreed acceptance rules: a small change near the throat fixes how well the horn loads the driver. The single score number hides this, so the rules, not the score, decide.
Some design groups have plenty of results but still are not trustworthy enough to train the optimizer on. More of the same results would not fix that.
A coarser mesh on the back of the horn cuts the simulation size by about 22% on the tested shape types while beamwidths move by at most 0.16°; it does nothing for CAD-built horns.
The design with the best single score in this group fails an acceptance rule. Ranking by score alone would have picked the wrong design.
A planning document is out of date: it says a check is still to do, but the records show it was run and passed for a limited trial.
Some groups of results were produced with different versions of the simulation software, so they should be checked before being treated as one consistent set.
All numbers come from computer simulations, not from measuring real hardware. Nothing on this page starts any work by itself.
